title: PROPOSED CriterionCategory illustrative mock-record design
description: Transcribed from docs/product-truth/mock-data/leafcutter/criterion-categories.mock.json entities.CriterionCategory.fields (decision dec-93c1c730463c1f3c). All listed fields are present in every complete mock record. replaces and member_view are derived display views and source is fixture provenance; none of the three is a field of the record file. No reader, writer, index or runtime validator for category records exists yet; cross-record invariants (membership, label uniqueness, lifecycle rules) are stated in the dataset and are not expressed here.

id.description: string — kernel-minted cat-<16 hex>; stable for the life of the category (a label edit, merge or split never changes it)

repository_id.description: string — first part of the ADR-061 identity key (repository_id, kind, id); memory.repository_id from the kernel config

kind.description: enum: criterion_category — the declared record kind (ADR-061 key)

pref_label.description: string — the canonical question: a member's wording, or one the approving human wrote (SKOS prefLabel)

alt_labels.description: array of strings — the other wordings of the same question, from published records or mined traces (SKOS altLabel)

broader.description: string | null — id of the broader category this one narrows (SKOS broader)

replaced_by.description: array of category ids — set when this category is merged (one id) or split (several ids); empty while active

replaces.description: array of category ids — categories whose replaced_by names this one (derived reverse view for display, not a field of the record file)

members.description: array of { decision_id: dec id, criterion_id } — membership, stored only here, so published decision records stay unchanged

member_view.description: array of { decision_id, criterion_id, priority: required | supporting, question } — each member joined with its criterion from the decision record (derived display view, not a field of the record file)

decision_types.description: array of decision_type values the category applies to (declared vocabulary filter)

components.description: array of component ids from docs/components.json ([] == not limited to a component)

lifecycle_stage.description: enum: candidate | staged | published | retired — candidate == proposed by the offline mining job, awaiting a human; staged == approved in a kernel run and written to that run's root; published == entered into Git by a human-run publish; retired == published, then merged or split (replaced_by set)

approval_status.description: enum: proposed | approved — only a human approval turns a candidate into a record

proposed_by.description: string — criteria_mining (the offline mining job) or human:<name>

proposed_at.description: string — ISO-8601 UTC time the category was proposed

approved_by.description: string | null — human:<name>; never a model or the mining job; null while candidate

approved_at.description: string | null — ISO-8601 UTC time of the human approval of this version of the record; null while candidate

run_id.description: string | null — the kernel run that last staged this record (run-<16 hex>); null while candidate

staged_path.description: string | null — where that run staged the record; <run_root> is the machine-local kernel run root

record_path.description: string | null — docs/criteria/<id>.yaml once published (folder name not fixed by dec-93c1c730463c1f3c); null while candidate or staged

retirement.description: object | null — { retired_at, retired_by: human:<name>, reason } written when a human merges or splits the category; null while active

usage_count.description: integer | null — distinct published decisions among members; generated from published records into a generated index (like docs/decisions/index.json), never hand-written; null while candidate or staged

mined_from.description: array of sightings the offline mining job found; Langfuse is read only by that job, never by a decision run

source.description: string — where this sample record comes from: real data it is grounded in, and what is illustrative (fixture provenance, not a record field)
